extracted.intended_audience: general magazine fiction readers and aspiring creative writers
extracted.subtask_description: Short magazine-style fiction that models themes about artistic craft and the maker's relationship to ephemeral work; useful for writers studying how a story communicates creative-moral principles. Focus is on narrative prose and craft-related aphorisms embedded in fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient unto eternity is the glory of the hour
rubrics_metrics.description: "Sufficient unto eternity is the glory of the hour." (ephemeral works can still achieve full artistic value if masterly done)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The narrator/old man argues that even fleeting performances or perishable arts possess a higher joy when the work is "right, was masterly done" — that there is satisfaction and artistic legitimacy in a transient triumph, likened to a sunset or a light on the water.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose a durable medium if you seek permanence
rubrics_metrics.description: "Paint, chisel, then, or write if you wish your work to endure." (media choice affects longevity of the work)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrast is drawn between moving pictures (Bernhardt) and 'permanent' arts; if an artist's goal is endurance, select media historically more lasting (painting, sculpture, writing) rather than ephemeral forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Big-'W' Work vs work-with-a-little-'w'
rubrics_metrics.description: Big-'W' Work: "Work you love for the Work's sake." work-with-a-little-'w': mechanical paid labor done only for pay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Voice distinguishes intrinsic creative work (Big-'W') that requires devotion, brings love and joy but little money, and is often ephemeral, from the routine paid work that sustains life. It prescribes acknowledging both: one must often mix practical paid labor with periods devoted to Big-'W' projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Big-'W' must be done by hand / thumb-and-craft
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Big-'W' Work you love to do must be done by hand. It can't be done any other way."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The story insists the highest craft requires manual skill and personal touch — 'that is why you were given thumbs' — arguing for hands-on workmanship and fine hand-craftsmanship rather than mechanized production for the most worthy creations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance livelihood and higher art (practical cycle of work)
rubrics_metrics.description: "You'll have to keep on at it somewhat — say, half your life at work-with-a-little-'w'..." (practical necessity to alternate paid work and creative work)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides creators to save resources during routine work periods so they can answer the call to devote time to Big-'W' projects later; implies seasonal/periodic dedication rather than full-time leisure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mastery, patience and reworking as a standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Mastery and painstaking reworking are necessary: the weaver spends days on tiny edging, remakes designs, and grows to be 'the finest hand-weaver.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text models sustained patience, repeated refinement, and pride in workmanship as the route to excellence — redoing, iterating, and attending to fine detail are praised as hallmarks of high-quality craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embrace impermanence while valuing the joy of creation
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Work will surely die as soon as you've accomplished it." (the work may vanish immediately but creates profound joy and meaning)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when creations are transient and ultimately discarded (Summer throws garments away), the emotional/spiritual reward ('the joy of good work well done', 'God whispering the secrets of life') justifies the labor; artistic worth isn't only in permanence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsiveness and speed under changing demands
rubrics_metrics.description: 'I'm in a dreadful hurry... please do be quick about it.' (client/subject-driven urgency and changing specifications)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The weaver must work 'as fast as his fingers could go' and adapt to last-minute changes (redesigns, color changes). This models the importance of responsiveness, flexibility, and the ability to execute fine work rapidly when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attention to color and sensory detail as a design criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeated focus on precise colors and sensory imagery (lemon-colored silk, apple-green tassels, 'bluer and bluer') as integral to the craft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The narrative highlights color choice and subtle sensory detail as essential to conveying beauty and character in crafted objects; selecting and layering color is presented as a deliberate aesthetic skill.
